scoring: Analyst-defined inherent exposure priority, not CVSS, attack likelihood or verified residual risk. Confidence concerns endpoint classification.

owasp.assessment_mode: Cross-cutting manual review; not automatically proven by URL discovery

rules.name: Credential stuffing
rules.scenario: Automated reuse of stolen account credentials against the authentication flow.
controls: Bot telemetry across the login page and submission endpoint
Risk-based MFA and account takeover monitoring
rules.validation: Use approved test accounts and identity logs to verify login controls and legitimate-user impact.

rules.name: Password spraying and credential cracking
rules.scenario: Distributed guessing or lockout abuse can target authentication without high per-IP volume.
controls: Account-aware throttling without easy lockout DoS
rules.validation: Review failure rates across accounts, lockout behavior and identity-provider coverage.

rules.name: Fake accounts and referral farming
rules.scenario: Automation can create accounts or consume onboarding/referral rewards at scale.
rules.validation: Confirm disposable-identity controls, legitimate signup rates and referral reward boundaries.

rules.name: Recovery abuse and reset flooding
rules.scenario: Recovery requests may be abused for token guessing, account discovery or notification flooding.
rules.validation: Review reset request and token validation separately; confirm that notifications cannot be flooded.

rules.name: OTP/SMS/voice pumping
rules.scenario: Automated requests can generate paid messages or calls and exhaust delivery budgets.
controls: Provider spend limits and resend cooldowns
rules.validation: Verify destination quotas, resend windows, spending caps and monitoring with the application owner.

rules.name: OTP and verification-token guessing
rules.scenario: Automated token attempts can attack short verification or authentication codes.
controls: Attempt limits bound to identity and transaction
rules.validation: Confirm code entropy, attempt limits, expiry and server-side transaction binding.

rules.name: Carding and card cracking
rules.scenario: A payment or card-validation flow can be used to test stolen cards or guess missing card details.
rules.validation: Review gateway decline patterns and approved test-card procedures; do not test real card data.

rules.name: Cashing out and loyalty theft
rules.scenario: Compromised accounts or stolen value can be converted into purchases, transfers or rewards.
rules.validation: Confirm transaction limits, step-up authentication, replay handling and the actual financial impact.

rules.name: Scalping
rules.scenario: Automation may gain unfair access to limited tickets, products, bookings or appointments.
rules.validation: Validate scarcity, legitimate queue behavior and limits per customer across sessions.

rules.name: Denial of inventory
rules.scenario: Repeated holds or abandoned reservations can make stock or appointments unavailable.
rules.validation: Check inventory-hold lifecycle, maximum concurrent reservations and automatic release.

rules.name: Content, price and data scraping
rules.scenario: Automated harvesting can collect commercial content, prices, availability or large data sets.
controls: Identity quotas with verified good-bot exceptions
rules.validation: Identify valuable data, acceptable crawlers, data licensing and normal pagination volumes.

rules.name: Coupon and gift-card enumeration
rules.scenario: Repeated code or balance lookups can discover valid promotional or stored-value tokens.
rules.validation: Review token entropy, lookup response differences and per-identity redemption limits.

rules.name: Spam and message abuse
rules.scenario: Automated submissions can distribute spam, poison content or flood inboxes and support queues.
rules.validation: Check recipients, publication behavior, moderation and notification fan-out.

rules.name: Metric and reputation manipulation
rules.scenario: Repeated automated interactions can alter reviews, rankings, engagement or other business metrics.
rules.validation: Validate uniqueness rules and how submitted events affect business metrics.

rules.name: Paid-service and advertising cost inflation
rules.scenario: Bots can consume chargeable advertising, messaging, compute or AI services.
controls: Bound expensive work to authenticated entitlements
rules.validation: Document unit cost, normal consumption, budget caps and abuse alerting.

rules.name: Application resource exhaustion
rules.scenario: Automated expensive requests may consume compute, storage, database or upstream capacity.
rules.validation: Review expensive operations, timeout budgets and capacity without running load tests.

rules.name: Auction sniping
rules.scenario: Automation can submit precisely timed bids near auction close.
rules.validation: Confirm auction timing rules and what constitutes unfair automated bidding.

rules.name: Expediting and workflow automation
rules.scenario: Automation may accelerate workflows, collect rewards or bypass expected participation.
rules.validation: Confirm required steps and server-side enforcement of workflow order and rewards.

rules.name: Account aggregation
rules.scenario: Intermediary automation may collect or interact with multiple accounts, legitimately or abusively.
rules.validation: Distinguish permitted aggregators and customer consent from unauthorized automated access.

rules.name: Account and object enumeration
patterns: \b(check user|check email|email available|username available|user exists|lookup|tracking|order status|pnr)\b
rules.scenario: Repeated lookups can identify accounts, bookings or other business objects.
rules.validation: Compare response behavior using approved test data and verify object authorization; bot protection cannot repair authorization flaws.

rules.name: API token and session abuse
rules.scenario: Automated token requests, refreshes or repeated session creation can abuse identity services.
rules.validation: Identify client credentials versus user authentication and protect the correct grant/refresh flow.

rules.name: GraphQL batching and operation abuse
rules.scenario: One GraphQL URL can expose many operations; batching, aliases or costly resolvers may amplify automation.
controls: Pagination bounds and authorization at resolvers
rules.validation: Inventory actual operations and validate cost, depth, alias and batch limits; no introspection or mutation is sent by BotScope.

rules.name: Upload and storage abuse
rules.scenario: Automated submissions can exhaust storage or distribute unwanted content.
rules.validation: Confirm storage costs, ownership, moderation and cleanup behavior.

rules.name: Webhook and callback abuse
rules.scenario: Repeated or replayed callbacks can trigger unnecessary work or business actions.
rules.validation: Confirm sender verification and idempotency; interactive browser challenges are usually unsuitable.

rules.name: Realtime channel abuse
rules.scenario: Automated channel creation or messages may exhaust connections or amplify application work.
rules.validation: Confirm transport and long-lived session controls; discovery does not test WebSocket messages.
